caption: The drawing depicts an architectural window set in a wall. The window is rectangular with a rounded arch at the top, composed of blue-grey stone blocks forming the arch and the sides. The wooden window shutters, colored in light brown with visible wood grain, are partially open, revealing a white interior window frame that has a subtle, vertical grey border and thin red decorative patterns. Below the window, there is a window ledge with alternating horizontal bands of color: a yellow band with a geometric looping pattern, a plain light yellow band, a thinner white band, and a wide reddish-brown band with a swirling pattern. The composition is centered, with the window and wall details occupying most of the space and a blank off-white background surrounding the scene. The artist's signature "Norman Hecks" appears in red at the lower right corner.
title: South Wall of "Governor's Room" at Mission
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
